newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's June industrial activity up 12.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's June industrial activity up 12.0 pct.

text.p: Mexico's overall industrial activity in June grew 12.0 percent compared with the same month in 1995, partly fueled by a 13.2 percent increase in construction and a 12.6 percent rise in manufacturing, the Finance Ministry said on Thursday.
In a Reuters survey, analysts had on average expected a rise of 12.31 percent in industrial activity.
It was the fifth straight monthly rise in the indicator and all the main divisions strengthened.
Mining was up 7.6 percent from June 1995, the Finance Ministry said, reflecting gains of 7.8 percent in oil-related activity and 7.3 percent in non-oil mining areas.
The 12.6 percent rise in manufacturing included a 13.5 percent jump in the maquiladora export sector.
A sectoral breakdown gave the following results:
Textiles, clothing and leather output +22.9 pct
Wood and wood products +13.5 pct
Paper, paper products, printing +3.7 pct
Oil-based chemicals, rubber, plastics +1.4 pct
Non-metallic minerals, ex-oil and coal +18.6 pct
Basic metals +25.1 pct
Metal products, machinary and equipment +30.2 pct
"Other manufacturing industries" +12.8 pct
Food, beverages and tobacco -0.4 pct
Manufacturing output was directed as follows:
Durable and non-durable consumer goods +5.6 pct
Capital goods +42.1 pct
Intermediate goods +13.0 pct

Construction activity was up 13.2 percent, especially driven by increases in electricity, commmunications, oil and petrochemicals. Also, the production of materials used in the construction industry such as cement grew.
Generation of electricity, gas and water was up 5.4 percent in June compared with the same month in 1994, the Finance Ministry said.
-- Henry Tricks, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9560
